content: Sanguisorba officinalis, commonly known as Great Burnet, is a plant that belongs to the Rosaceae family and the Rosoideae subfamily. It is indigenous to the cooler regions of the Northern Hemisphere, including Europe, northern Asia, and northern North America. This plant is a herbaceous perennial that can grow up to 1 meter in height and is typically found in grasslands, thriving particularly well on grassy banks. The plant has several commercial applications. Its extensive root system is utilized for erosion control and as a bioremediator, particularly in the reclamation of degraded sites such as landfills. The leaves of Sanguisorba officinalis are edible and are often used in salads due to their mild flavor, which is reminiscent of cucumber. To enhance leaf production, selective pruning of the apical meristems, such as those at the flower heads, is performed. In ethnomedicine, Sanguisorba officinalis has been a staple in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for thousands of years. Its use is thought to be influenced by the doctrine of signatures, particularly as a treatment for conditions involving bleeding. The root of the plant is specifically employed to manage bloody dysentery and nosebleeds. Additionally, it is applied topically to treat burns and insect bites.
